teams.heading: Jake White named Fiji head coach, replacing interim Senirusi Seruvakula
teams.body: Jake White's appointment as Fiji head coach, made last week, hands him a side ranked 10th in the world that has lost four of five Tests this year. He replaces interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula after a field of 31 applicants, and Fiji face Japan this weekend before Nations Championship games against France, Ireland and Italy in November. Former Bulls backline coach Chris Rossouw says he would not be surprised if Fiji surprise people, while Willem Strauss said: "I think Fiji needs its South African discipline."

lead.why: The White hire is the only national-side item left on the shortlist, so it is framed as last week's appointment rather than fresh news.

teams.heading: Dan Cole fears Prem's attacking style leaves England exposed against Australia
teams.body: Former England prop Dan Cole has admitted he is anxious that the Prem's attacking emphasis is leaving England's players short of Test rugby. Speaking on the For the Love of Rugby podcast, Cole said the league's style does not translate to international rugby, citing the attritional, breakdown-heavy nature of recent Tests. With Steve Borthwick's side due to face Australia at Twickenham, Cole's concern is that England go into the autumn without Test-match rugby behind them.

lead.why: A fresh men's item on England's Test preparation, not a rehash of the Feyi-Waboso or Northampton stories already run.

teams.heading: Pau club's Théo Attissogbe inspires 41-17 Champions Cup win over Leicester
teams.body: Club side Pau's 41-17 win over Leicester Tigers at Stade du Hameau in the Investec Champions Cup was a statement, with France star Théo Attissogbe central to it. The hosts trailed 10-3 after 18 minutes, led 17-10 at half-time and then scored 24 points to Leicester's seven after the break. Axel Desperes added 16 points off the boot, and the five-two try count earned Pau a bonus point.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item not already run, and it is the one France fans will talk about: a French star's display in a Champions Cup win.

teams.heading: Jack Conan's shoulder injury needs further assessment before Farrell names Ireland squad
teams.body: Leinster say Jack Conan's shoulder injury, which forced him off in the win over Clermont Auvergne, still needs further assessment, and the timing is awkward for Andy Farrell. Caelan Doris is expected to miss the November window after a knee infection delayed his recovery from surgery, so a prolonged Conan absence would leave Ireland without both first-choice number 8s. Leo Cullen initially said Conan would be out for a little while, with the full extent due within a week. Farrell names his squad on Wednesday.

lead.why: A fresh injury doubt to a back-row option, landing days before Farrell names his November squad, with Caelan Doris already out.

teams.heading: Club: Ex-Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie set for Glasgow Warriors debut against Benetton
teams.body: In club news, Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has come to unleash Jamie Ritchie, the 63-cap former Scotland captain, for his Warriors debut in Saturday's URC match against Benetton in Treviso. Back in full training after ankle and Achilles problems and summer surgery, Ritchie is expected to play this weekend, and Carolan frames the timing as useful before Scotland's Nations Cup, a couple of weeks away. He signed from Perpignan in the summer after 11 years at Edinburgh.

lead.why: It is the freshest new item on the list, and Ritchie's first Glasgow appearance also bears on Scotland's autumn plans.

teams.heading: Ben Whitehouse joins Steve Tandy's Wales staff as full-time specialist coach
teams.body: Steve Tandy has borrowed a page from Rassie Erasmus's playbook. The WRU announced on Monday that Ben Whitehouse has joined the men's national squad full-time as a specialist coach, working with coaches and players on law, discipline, decision-making and communication. The 36-year-old is set to hang up his whistle after Saturday's URC clash between the Ospreys and Dragons in Swansea, and the model echoes South Africa's appointment of Jaco Peyper as laws adviser in 2024.

lead.why: A new full-time national-squad coaching hire, which is more directly about Wales's own set-up than the Williams, late-claims or Faletau pieces.

teams.heading: Argentina's England defeat stays at heart of TMO row before November
teams.body: England's win over Argentina remains the reference point for a TMO row that is still open. Dave Rennie is set to raise the controversy at World Rugby's November officials meeting, and the BBC's match headline called the game 'Chaos' and 'comedy refereering'. A separate Springboks-Wallabies iPhone TMO saga is being framed as a major red flag ahead of the 2027 World Cup. Nothing in the reporting so far says what the November meeting will change, so Argentina's stake stays unresolved until World Rugby publishes new guidance.

teams.heading: Desiree Miller scores twice as women's Wallaroos thrash Scotland 56-12 in Sydney
teams.body: Australia's women's side, the Wallaroos, ran in eight tries in a 56-12 WXV Global Series win over Scotland in Sydney, leading 35-5 at the break. Desiree Miller and Amelia Whitaker both scored twice, with Brittany Merlo, Maya Stewart, Ellis and Eva Karpani also crossing. Scotland, under caretaker head coach Dave Butcher, lost Sarah Bonar to illness shortly before kick-off, and have now lost eight straight, four of them in the new competition.

lead.why: The only genuinely new item in the pack, and it is labelled as women's rugby; the men's Bledisloe coverage is already-read follow-up.

teams.heading: Japan women's sevens retain Asia Rugby title with undefeated campaign in Colombo
teams.body: Japan's women's sevens side beat China 14-7 in the Colombo final to defend the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series title, finishing undefeated across the leg. The Sakura Sevens, who finished with the maximum 40 series points, head to HSBC SVNS, where Japan are already competing. Head coach Yuka Kanematsu said she was "truly proud" of the players, five of them making debuts. The men's side also won Leg 2, beating Hong Kong China 28-14 in the final, but Hong Kong China kept the series on points difference.

lead.why: It is the only new Japan item in the pack, corroborated by two outlets, and it is a clear result story.

teams.heading: Ardie Savea and Ruben Love definitely miss All Blacks' end-of-year tour
teams.body: Ardie Savea and Ruben Love will definitely miss the end-of-year tour, and Leroy Carter is definitely out of the northern leg, Planet Rugby reports. Richie Mo'unga is a doubt for the Nations Championship. Mils Muliaina, on The Breakdown, says the depth is being tested and he thinks Dave Rennie has the stock to cope, while Brad Weber judges the drop-off from Love is not big. Peter Lakai and Wallace Sititi combined well at the weekend.

lead.why: It is a new injury story on the national squad, and it reaches beyond the Bledisloe result that the edition has already covered.

teams.heading: Tony Brown reveals Erasmus' late call and says Boks have everything right
teams.body: Springbok attack coach Tony Brown has told John Plumtree's Plumtree Uncut podcast that Rassie Erasmus first made contact after the 2023 World Cup, then went quiet until Christmas, before finally coming back with an offer. Brown says he signed straight away, with Argentina's Felipe Contepomi also having wanted him. He praised the talent pipeline, pointing to South Africa's run of U20 tournament wins as evidence that the country has got its development right.

lead.why: A new coach reaction on the national side, which the editor notes rank above the Wales, Ulster and already-reported club items.
